This confirms everything needed. No server-side delete call exists on slot deletion.

## Login
`AuthService.login(username)` ([auth.service.ts](frontend/src/app/services/auth.service.ts)) — no password/server call. It checks `localStorage['ai_dnd_user_<lowercase name>']`; if found, loads that `UserProfile`, else creates a fresh one `{username, campaigns: []}` and persists it. The active profile is also mirrored to `localStorage['ai_dnd_user']`. `login.component.ts`'s `login()` calls this, then routes to `/characters` if `campaigns.length === 0`, else shows saved campaign slots.

## Campaign storage
Campaigns live only in the browser, inside the `UserProfile.campaigns` array (`CampaignSlot[]`), persisted as JSON under `localStorage` keys `ai_dnd_user_<name>` (per-user) and `ai_dnd_user` (active copy). Each `CampaignSlot` holds a `sessionId`/`characterId` pointer into the Worker's D1/KV data — there is no server-side "campaign" table.

## Deleting a campaign slot
`login.component.ts`'s `deleteCampaign()` → `AuthService.removeCampaign(slotId)` just does `p.campaigns = p.campaigns.filter(c => c.slotId !== slotId)` and re-persists to `localStorage`. **It makes no HTTP call.** The server-side character (D1 `characters` row) and its KV session (`session:<id>`, see `worker/src/services/session.ts`) are untouched — they remain in D1/KV with nothing in the browser pointing to them anymore (confirmed by `auth.service.md`'s documented rule: "`removeCampaign` only deletes the slot. It doesn't delete the character on the server.").
